name: Cloforex

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Germany and Sweden, first in 1969 — for breathing problems and heart harm

similar.name: Clofibrate
problems: Pulled from the market in Israel and 2 other countries, first in 1979 — for blood vessel problems and cancer risk

similar.name: Beclobrate
problems: Pulled from the market in Switzerland, first in 1990 — for liver harm

similar.name: Chlorphentermine
problems: Pulled from the market in Germany and Venezuela, first in 1967 — for breathing problems and heart harm

summary: Cloforex was pulled from the market in Germany and Sweden, beginning in 1969, because of damage to breathing and the heart [3]. In addition, a small computer model rather than human testing estimated that the drug has low risk scores of 35 for the liver and 45 for the heart [M]. Several similar drugs were also withdrawn from various countries due to harms such as liver damage, heart damage, breathing problems, blood vessel harm, and carcinogenicity, which is the ability to cause cancer [3].
